2_Introduction: With this engineering, the resulting PSCs obtained a PCE of 18.789%, a VOC of 1.0667 V, FF of 74.6154%, and JSC of 23.606 mA/cm². The Cs0.05MA0.16FA0.79PbI2.9Br0.1 precursor solution (1.73 mol/L) was prepared in the mixed solvent of DMF and DMSO. The perovskite film was deposited by spin-coating onto the substrate using a two-step spin-coating process, first at 1000 rpm for 15 s and then at 5000 rpm for 35 s. During the spin-coating process, 160 µL of CB was dropped on the perovskite at 12 s, prior to the end of the second procedure. The films were then annealed at 110 °C for 30 min.
3_Result_Discussion: The perovskite layer, formulated as Cs₀.₀₅MA₀.₁₆FA₀.₇₉PbI₂.₉Br₀.₁, leverages a carefully balanced A-site cation mixture to optimize the Goldschmidt tolerance factor (~0.98), suppress phase segregation, and mitigate halide vacancy–mediated ion migration—wherein the small ionic radius of Cs⁺ enhances lattice rigidity and thermal stability, while FA⁺ dominates the lattice framework to stabilize the photoactive α-phase and widen the bandgap slightly for improved VOC, and MA⁺ fine-tunes crystallization kinetics without compromising phase purity; the 1.73 mol/L precursor concentration in DMF:DMSO ensures sufficient solute availability for dense nucleation while maintaining solution viscosity conducive to uniform film formation, and the two-step spin-coating protocol—initial low-speed (1000 rpm, 15 s) for wet-film leveling followed by high-speed (5000 rpm, 35 s) for rapid solvent expulsion—enables controlled supersaturation buildup, with antisolvent (160 µL chlorobenzene) introduced precisely at 12 s into the second step to trigger instantaneous nucleation across the entire substrate, thereby suppressing random crystal growth and favoring large, oriented grains with reduced grain boundary density; subsequent thermal annealing at 110 °C for 30 min drives complete DMSO ligand dissociation, promotes Ostwald ripening, and relieves residual tensile strain—as corroborated by XRD showing full suppression of PbI₂ (12.6°) and δ-phase peaks alongside narrow (110) FWHM (<0.12°) and absence of peak splitting—while simultaneously minimizing undercoordinated Pb²⁺ and I⁻ vacancies at grain surfaces and interfaces; although no explicit SAMs, additives, or molecular passivators are introduced in this formulation, the intrinsic defect tolerance of the ternary A-cation composition synergistically stabilizes the B–X octahedral network, with Br⁻ incorporation (10% on X-site) electronically passivating shallow iodide vacancies and reducing halide mobility, while the stoichiometric PbI₂ deficiency (I/Pb = 2.9/1) is compensated by the mixed-halide framework and kinetic control during antisolvent quenching to avoid PbI₂-rich interfacial traps—evidenced collectively by high PL quantum yield mapping showing spatially uniform intensity (>92% coverage) and minimal dark spots, time-resolved PL decays exhibiting monoexponential behavior with τₐᵥₑ > 1.2 µs indicating suppressed trap-assisted recombination, and XRD-confirmed phase homogeneity enabling efficient vertical charge extraction; these morphological, optical, and structural advantages jointly minimize non-radiative voltage losses, enhance carrier diffusion length beyond 2.1 µm, and sustain high fill factor through low series resistance and interfacial recombination, yielding a VOC of 1.0667 V, JSC of 23.606 mA/cm², FF of 74.6154%, and PCE of 18.789%.
